Beta hosting decided by Owner (2026-11-02): Cloudflare Workers Free runs the API and web UI; Neon Free provides PostgreSQL, reached from Workers through Hyperdrive Free; Supabase was evaluated and kept as a fully compatible alternative. Portability rules are binding: (1) only deploy/cloudflare/src/entry.py knows about Cloudflare - no Cloudflare-proprietary APIs (D1/KV/Durable Objects) in core logic; (2) persistence uses standard SQL and widely-available PostgreSQL extensions only, no Neon/Supabase platform extras (their Auth/Storage/Realtime) in the product core; (3) the app stays stateless, all durable state in PostgreSQL; daily development and tests use a local database, Neon is reserved for the shared beta/staging environments (separate Neon project per environment, compute kept at the 0.25 CU minimum). Rationale: the whole beta stack costs 0; PostgreSQL-to-PostgreSQL migration between Neon and Supabase, or out to a VPS/AWS/Azure/GCP running the same ASGI app under uvicorn, stays a pg_dump/pg_restore operation. Deployment packaging prepared in deploy/cloudflare/ with runbook docs/DEPLOY_CLOUDFLARE_NEON.md; actual deployment awaits the Owner's Cloudflare and Neon accounts. DEPLOYED 2026-11-02: the API is live at https://iaict-core-platform.iaict-coreplatform-mhy.workers.dev (Cloudflare account subdomain iaict-coreplatform-mhy; deployed via uv run pywrangler deploy after the browser-OAuth route failed on wrangler's ~2-minute authorization window and the Owner chose the one-time API-token route; the token was used transiently and never stored). Live verification: /health 200 with env=beta, deny-by-default 400/403/503 responses, tenant creation 201 with a temporary platform secret that was deleted right after the check (platform administration stays disabled at 503 until the Owner sets their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret). Verified platform constraint: in-memory state is per-isolate and is not shared between Worker requests, so multi-request flows only become meaningful when the T-004 PostgreSQL layer lands - as planned. PERSISTENCE WIRING (2026-11-02): the Owner created the Neon project (ap-southeast-1, PostgreSQL 18.6) and shared the direct connection string transiently (never stored). Verified from this environment over Neon's HTTPS SQL endpoint (the VM proxy intercepts raw TCP/5432): credentials valid, all 12 schema tables applied, cross-tenant FK rejection reproduced on Neon itself (SQLSTATE 23503). Worker-side driver settled by spike tests against Cloudflare's official Python+Hyperdrive guidance: asyncpg is recommended but its Pyodide wheel is served from a CDN unreachable from this build environment, and direct-to-Neon connections from Python Workers fail on TLS over the socket shim - which is exactly what Hyperdrive exists to solve (plaintext local leg, ssl=False). Chosen driver: pg8000 (pure Python, on Cloudflare's supported list). app/workerstore.py implements the store contract on pg8000; app/store.py gained a LazyWorkerStore selected by the Workers entrypoint (IAICT_BACKEND=hyperdrive) that binds the Hyperdrive config from the first request env and otherwise falls back to in-memory storage, reported openly by /health (storage field). Full suite passes 31/31 in all three modes (memory, psycopg, pg8000) against real PostgreSQL. The updated app is deployed to the beta (currently storage: memory). ONE step remains, with the Owner: create the Hyperdrive configuration - the current API token is denied Hyperdrive access (error 10000), so the Owner creates it in the dashboard (Workers & Pages -> Hyperdrive -> Create, name iaict-neon, direct Neon connection string) and shares the config id; then the binding is uncommented in wrangler.jsonc, the beta redeployed, and durable multi-request flows verified live. COMPLETED 2026-11-02: the Owner created the Hyperdrive config 'iaict-neon' (id 3cdbf0e61cfc4a078ea1f4790200a65f; direct connection string without channel_binding, caching disabled) in the dashboard; the binding is active in wrangler.jsonc and the beta now runs DURABLE: /health reports storage 'postgresql-hyperdrive'. Live verification with a temporary platform secret (deleted afterwards): tenant beta-pilot created in one request was fully usable in later requests - bootstrap admin, zone Z-01, mother plant MPL-001 referencing the zone, crop plan PLAN-2026 - with 5 audit entries readable through the API; records cross-checked present in Neon. One transient 500 on a list call was traced to the cached per-isolate connection pattern; WorkerPgStore now opens a fresh connection per operation (Cloudflare's prescribed Hyperdrive pattern) and repeated spaced calls all return 200. Seed records (beta-pilot tenant with its zone/plant/plan) intentionally remain in Neon as the beta's first real data. Platform administration stays disabled until the Owner sets their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret. URL CHANGE + ADMIN KEY (2026-11-02): the Owner renamed the account workers.dev subdomain from 'iaict-coreplatform-mhy' to 'mihy' - the canonical beta URL is now https://iaict-core-platform.mihy.workers.dev and the old URL no longer resolves; all data was unaffected (it lives in Neon, verified: beta-pilot records intact at the new address). The Owner also set their own PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY secret (verified active from outside: a wrong key now returns 401 PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID instead of 503).

Supabase trial executed at the Owner's direction (2026-11-02): the beta's Hyperdrive binding now points at a Supabase PostgreSQL project (Singapore, direct connection, config 'iaict-supabase' id 4ee90fdeba69436493d69e11fd7a870b); the schema was auto-created by the Worker on first request and the beta-pilot dataset was rebuilt from an API snapshot (tenant, Pilot Admin, zones Z-01 + Z-TMP, plant MPL-001, plan PLAN-2026). Neon (config 'iaict-neon') is untouched and remains the instant rollback. Measured result: latency improved (successful calls 5-6s vs 7-10s) but the failure rate did NOT improve (sequential 8/20, dashboard-parallel 19/48 - same class as Neon: 1101/1102/dropped connections). wrangler tail evidence (14 sampled requests: 9 ok, 4 canceled by the runtime's hang detector, 1 exceededCpu; successful requests burn ~1.2-1.9s CPU each) identifies the bottleneck as the Cloudflare Python Workers runtime itself (Pyodide + synchronous pg8000), not the database. DEC-006 is therefore amended in part: the database may be Neon or Supabase interchangeably, but the API runtime is expected to move to a plain always-on host (T-013) running the same ASGI app under uvicorn with the psycopg backend - the portability rules of DEC-006 are what make this a packaging change, not a rewrite. The Owner also forgot their PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEY; a temporary secret was used to create the tenant on Supabase and deleted immediately after, so platform administration is disabled (503) until the Owner sets a fresh key of their own choosing.

Owner decision 2026-11-03: adopt Cloudflare D1 as the beta's store on Workers (T-014), superseding the T-013 plain-host relocation. This AMENDS DEC-006 in one respect: a Cloudflare-proprietary API (D1) now sits behind the store boundary. The rest of DEC-006's portability discipline is kept and is what bounds the lock-in: the store interface is storage-agnostic, the PostgreSQL backends (psycopg + pg8000/Hyperdrive) remain in the tree and green in tests, the datasets on Supabase and Neon are untouched, and wrangler.jsonc documents the rollback (restore the Hyperdrive binding + IAICT_BACKEND=hyperdrive + redeploy). Rationale is measured, not preferential: on the same free Python Workers runtime, D1 scored sequential 20/20 + parallel 48/48 with cpuTime median ~26-42ms per request, versus 8/20 + 19/48 at ~1,241ms CPU on PostgreSQL via Hyperdrive; the hang-cancellations and exceededCpu failures disappeared entirely. D1 was also verified to enforce the composite (tenant_id, ref_id) foreign keys the tenant isolation model relies on (cross-tenant INSERT rejected, SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY).

Owner decision 2026-11-03: adopt the Vietnamese agri-forestry-fishery traceability data standard (research dossier, 33 tables + 3 views; ND 38/2026, NQ 36/2026, TCVN 11892-1:2026, TT 02/2024/TT-BKHCN, TCVN 12850:2019, GS1) as the platform's data-model reference, recorded as SRS delta D-STD-01. Adoption is phased: phase 1 (T-015) covers the crop-chain core that maps onto the SRS ZON/MPL/FLD/LOT groups; the packing chain, national-portal sync, transport/recall and the forestry/livestock/fishery specializations are phase 2, sequenced with the pilot milestones. The standard's PostgreSQL/PostGIS/bitemporal forms are adapted to the platform's tenant-scoped composite-FK model behind the existing store boundary; enforcement rules (PHI gate, mass balance) live at the API layer so they hold identically on every backend.

tasks.title: Fix stuck-at-connecting login + tenant picker on the sign-in screen
tasks.evidence: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-11-02: the Owner reported the sign-in only ever showed the connecting state. The setup overlay is styled .setup{display:flex} in author CSS, which overrides the UA [hidden]{display:none} rule - so setting hidden=true after a successful sign-in never actually hid the overlay, and the button kept its 'connecting' label forever. The same flaw kept the inline error banner permanently displayed. Fix: a global [hidden]{display:none !important} rule. Also added per Owner request: a tenant picker on the sign-in screen (button reads the platform key typed into the form - tenant listing stays platform-privileged - renders tenant cards; tapping one fills the tenant and loads its accounts), and a 20s AbortController timeout on all API calls so a stalled network surfaces an error instead of an endless spinner. DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-11-02: sign-in page now 4232 bytes with the tenant-picker markup, served CSS contains the [hidden] fix, served app.js contains loadTenants + AbortController, /health unchanged (postgresql-hyperdrive).

tasks.title: Fix intermittent dashboard data failures under parallel load (Hyperdrive/pg8000)
tasks.evidence: Found by the new browser-test rule (Owner instruction 2026-11-02): the first real-browser test passed sign-in but the dashboard failed with a generic error, although curl checks were green. Diagnosis chain, all evidenced: (1) the dashboard's four parallel list calls intermittently hit Cloudflare 1102 (Worker CPU limit) - crop-plans reproduced returning 503 'error code: 1102' while sibling endpoints returned 200; the old all-or-nothing Promise.all turned one failure into a full-page error. (2) A first fix (cached per-isolate pg8000 connection) exposed a deeper bug in wrangler tail: SQLSTATE 26000 'unnamed prepared statement does not exist' - Hyperdrive rebalances upstream sessions at transaction boundaries and pg8000's PARSE/DESCRIBE split across them. Final fix set: WorkerPgStore reuses one connection per isolate with SELECT 1 health-check + drop-on-error, every operation runs in ONE explicit transaction (autocommit off) so Hyperdrive pins the upstream session, and unique-violation handling moved outside the session (pg8000 refuses statements in a failed transaction - 3 local tests caught this before deploy). UI: GETs retry once on network/5xx; dashboard and plans views load sections independently (allSettled) with a per-section warning instead of a full-page error. Verification: full suite green in all three store modes; live parallel load 14/16 immediate 200 with the rest absorbed by the UI retry and NO 26000/500s; live write flow 201 + duplicate 409 CODE_EXISTS; post-fix real-browser re-test PASSED - dashboard rendered stats 2/1/1/0 (zones/plants/plans/lots), zones page listed Z-01 + Z-TMP, plans page listed PLAN-2026, no error states, and the remembered session persisted across browser restarts. Known leftovers: free-tier latency is still seconds per request and an occasional 503 can appear under parallel load (absorbed by retry); a clearly-labeled test zone Z-TMP created during write verification remains in beta-pilot (no delete endpoint yet). Process note: the browser agent's structural findings (counts, error presence) matched server data, but its decorative text details were partly paraphrased/invented - trust counts and states, verify labels against the API.

tasks.title: Fix residual dashboard intermittency: UI network-retry gap + WorkerPgStore round-trip diet
tasks.evidence: Owner chose investigation over a Supabase switch (2026-11-02). Controlled live measurement (read-only, browser-UA probe cross-checked with curl): sequential success only 8/20, dashboard-parallel 15/48; successful DB calls cost 7-10s warm or cold; /health (no DB) 0.3-3.4s bimodal by isolate warmth; failures were Cloudflare 1102 (free-tier resource limit), 1101 (Worker exception) and mid-stream connection drops. Neon scale-to-zero ruled out as the main cause: first call after >10 min idle cost the same 7.8-9.8s as warm calls. Code-verified cost structure: each list request ran >=2 store sessions (tenant guard + list), each with ping + query + COMMIT over Hyperdrive, and every fresh isolate replayed the full schema DDL on its first connection. UI bug found in app.js: api() retried only ApiError (HTTP) failures, never fetch-level network/timeout failures - exactly the failure class that defeated the dashboard retry in the 20:27 recheck. Fixes built: app.js GET retry = 3 attempts with 700/1600ms backoff covering network errors; WorkerPgStore per-isolate tenant/user cache (30s positive / 10s negative, writes invalidate), optimistic reads (no ping, one retry on a fresh connection - self-heal verified by killing the cached backend server-side), schema probe = one SELECT instead of full DDL. Tests: 30 passed + 1 skip (memory), 31/31 (psycopg), 31/31 (pg8000 worker mode) on real PostgreSQL 18.6; app.js passes node --check. Deployment pending the Owner's Cloudflare API token. DEPLOYED 2026-11-02 (Worker version b597ad4f) together with the Supabase switch. Live re-measurement with the same probe design: sequential 8/20 (unchanged), dashboard-parallel 19/48 (was 15/48), successful-call latency 5-6s (was 7-10s). Browser re-test (22:31-22:32 +07): sign-in fast, detail pages fine, dashboard still intermittent per section (first load 2 of 4 stats, one retry recovered zones but plans regressed, lots never rendered its 0). Verdict: the T-012 changes help latency and UI resilience but do NOT resolve the intermittency, whose cause sits in the Workers Python runtime (see DEC-007); follow-up is T-013.

tasks.title: Relocate the API runtime from Cloudflare Python Workers to a plain always-on host (uvicorn + psycopg), keeping Supabase/Neon as the database

tasks.evidence: SPIKE MEASURED 2026-11-02 (separate throwaway Worker 'iaict-d1-spike', same Cloudflare account/runtime, D1 database id 956d373b-5f72-4413-bff0-af5513ded7ee): the /list pattern mirrors the real read path (tenant-guard lookup + list query, two sequential awaited D1 queries, beta-pilot-equivalent data). Conclusion: the D1 leg removes the failure classes entirely on the same free Python Workers runtime. NOT yet proven: write load, the FastAPI framework overhead on top, D1 foreign-key enforcement (a load-bearing property verified on PostgreSQL), and the real dashboard pattern. Integration cost if adopted: the store boundary must become async (D1 has no synchronous API - the current sync pg8000 store cannot call it), the 12-table schema must be ported to the SQLite dialect, and DEC-006 must be amended (D1 is a Cloudflare-proprietary API; the PostgreSQL stores and the Supabase dataset stay in place as the documented exit path). Spike code lives outside the repo at ~/workspace/projects/iaict-d1-spike (not committed). Awaiting the Owner's choice between T-014 (D1 adoption), T-013 (plain-host relocation) or deferring. COMPLETED 2026-11-03: the whole store interface was made async; new D1Store (backend/app/d1store.py) runs the SQLite port of the 12-table schema (backend/app/schema_d1.sql, same composite FKs); InMemory/PgStore/WorkerPgStore converted with unchanged semantics. Test suite green in all four modes (memory 30+1 skip, D1-over-sqlite3-shim 30+1 skip, psycopg 31, pg8000 31). Deployed to the production D1 database 'iaict-core' (id f4d07d24-3375-4588-affc-f6122c440ca6), Worker version dfdbdfc3; /health reports storage 'd1'. beta-pilot was reseeded through the API with a temporary platform secret (deleted immediately after; platform admin verified back to 503 PLATFORM_DISABLED): tenant, Pilot Admin, Z-01, Z-TMP, MPL-001, PLAN-2026, audit consistent. Mandatory browser test (2026-11-03 02:29-02:30 +07): sign-in via account card, dashboard FIRST load complete at 2/1/1/0 with no warnings (lots rendered its 0 for the first time), zones and plans pages correct, reload again 2/1/1/0 clean. tasks.evidence: Owner directive 2026-11-03 with the research dossier (SHA-256 3afb2be6...cfeb1) recorded as delta D-STD-01 in pcs/SRS_CHANGES.md; full 33-table mapping in docs/DATA_MODEL.md (10 tables adopted in phase 1, remainder mapped to phase 2). Implemented: zones gain the PUC block (puc_code, puc_status, sector_category, market_scope, primary_species, scientific_name, issue_date, issuing_authority, post_inspect_due_date); new tenant-scoped kinds actors (ENT_ACTOR_HOUSEHOLD subset), spatial_units (ENT_SPATIAL_UNIT subset), zone_parcel_links (REL_ZONE_SPATIAL_UNIT, unique per tenant+zone+parcel), input_lots (ENT_INPUT_INVENTORY subset), phi_validations (LOG_PHI_VALIDATION); crop plans gain parcel link + variety + seed origin; field events gain input-lot link and computed safe_harvest_date = occurred date + PHI days; harvest lots gain farmer/parcel links + weigh slip, are rejected 400 PHI_VIOLATION when harvested before the plan's latest safe date (every attempt logged to phi_validations) and 400 MASS_BALANCE_EXCEEDED above the plan's target_yield_kg ceiling, and are stamped with traceability_code (plan | zone PUC-or-code | lot | harvest date, TT 02/2024) and data_retention_until (+12 months, TT 17/2021). Suite green in all four store modes: memory 37 passed + 1 skipped, D1-over-sqlite3-shim 37 + 1 skipped, psycopg 38, pg8000 38 (7 new tests in backend/tests/test_m3_traceability.py). D1 in-place upgrade path verified separately against a pre-T-015 schema copy (old data intact, new tables/columns appear, writes work) and then on production: deployed Worker version 871beb1e (2026-11-03), /health storage 'd1', remote D1 inspection shows all 5 new tables in database iaict-core, beta-pilot data intact (2 zones, 1 user, 1 plan, plus 1 lot the Owner created via the UI the same morning), new endpoints /api/v1/actors and /api/v1/phi-validations return 200 with empty lists. Mandatory browser test 2026-11-03 12:54-12:55 +07: sign-in via Pilot Admin card, dashboard 2/1/1/1 with no warnings, zones page 2 cards, lot create form contains the new farmer/parcel/weigh-slip fields, zone create form contains the PUC field, reload clean. UI: zone form/cards show PUC + primary species; lot form gained farmer code, parcel code, weigh slip; lot cards show farmer, weigh slip and traceability code. Phase 2 (packing chain PHC/SKU, national-portal traceability records + CTE stages, transport, recall, market approvals/GACC warnings, certifications, monitoring logs, livestock/fishery specializations) is mapped in docs/DATA_MODEL.md and not yet built.
